2147.desc: A red gem from a Laviente. Its huge size is enough to make anyone lost for words.

2148.desc: The thin hide of a Laviente. Surprisingly tough.

2149.desc: Laviente scales are so prized by Hunters that their theft is not unheard of.

2150.desc: A Laviente wing looks rather like a fin until you notice its enormous size.

2151.desc: Laviente marrow is housed in very thick bones, making it tough to extract.

2152.desc: The impressive girth of a Laviente horn is the stuff of legend.

2153.desc: A Laviente's fangs are the same size as its horns, and are harder than ore.

2154.desc: The tail of a Laviente. Heavy as lead, but its flexibility is unparalleled.

2155.desc: A Laviente's spike is really nothing more than a huge lump of bone.

2157.desc: A flawless natural crystal of a higher quality than the Blaster. Considered rare.

2158.desc: A wonderful natural crystal known as the "King of Blasters." Priceless.

2159.desc: Hard as bone, but easy to work with. Few in number, so considered precious.

2160.desc: A herb that can be crafted to act as a substitute for many rare materials.

2161.desc: This mushroom takes its name from the fact that it grows like granules on the ground.

2162.desc: After drying, this fruit makes an adorable rattling sound when shaken.

2163.desc: Rustles in the wind, and can be used as a dish, hence the name.

2164.desc: This mushroom takes its name from the fact that it grows like granules on the ground.

2165.desc: An opaque green mineral. Rarely found, and therefore highly prized.

2166.desc: A mineral with a stripy pattern that is totally unique.

2167.desc: The fossilized horn of a monster from ancient times. Extremely hard.

2168.desc: A pale pink crystal. Resists heat and impact. Pure ones fetch very high prices.

2169.desc: This mineral's mushroom-like shape is entirely natural.

2170.desc: A thin, flat mineral. Strong laterally, but breaks easily under downward force.

2171.desc: This insect's golden color makes it a popular charm for bringing luck with money.

2172.desc: Very slow-moving insect that looks just like the branch of a tree.

2173.desc: So named because its wing color and pattern look just like a Velociprey's hide.

2174.desc: Insect named for its circular red wings.

2175.desc: A butterfly named for the fact that its wings look like little green eyes.

2176.desc: An insect whose shape and color make it look exactly like a leaf.

2177.desc: Leaves worn by Shakalakas to cover their modesty. They're naked without them...

2178.desc: A stone crafted to have a circular surface. Pretty rough, but round enough.

2179.desc: An artificially curved piece of wood. Used when a sturdy material is required.

2180.desc: A well-used scrap of cloth that scarcely retains its original shape--or color.

2181.desc: A sliver of metal at the end of the handle is all that distinguishes it as a knife.

2182.desc: Made by thinly slicing a tree vertically. Sturdy if several layers are used.

2183.desc: A precious flower that only blooms one a year--if it blooms at all.

2184.desc: A berry that grows without much water. Makes you very thirsty when eaten.

2185.desc: Eats insects that come looking for nectar, which it doesn't even contain.

2186.desc: Not very tasty or suitable for crafting, but still worth gathering if you can.

2187.desc: This plant has nice, colorful flowers that stay in bloom for over a month.

2188.desc: Unlike the juicy fruit it produces, this plant's flowers are bright blue.

2189.desc: Very tough transparent mineral. Rarely found, so considered valuable.

2190.desc: Makes for a versatile material when refined. Made mainly of crystals.

2191.desc: Makes for a versatile material when refined. Made mainly of metal.

2192.desc: The forces of nature have smoothed its edges, making it appear rounded.

2193.desc: The forces of nature have smoothed its edges, making it look diamond-shaped.

2194.desc: The forces of nature have smoothed its edges, making it look star-shaped.

2195.desc: An insect with impressive pincers and horns. Be sure to approach it from behind.

2196.desc: Long, thin, and covered in a hard shell, this bug is ready for use as a nail.

2197.desc: Stores up sunlight during the daytime, letting it glow faintly in the night.

2198.desc: Part of a huge bug's shell. Looks and feels more like thick tree bark, though.

2199.desc: This insect is often seen on wet days, hence its name.
